output.brief: The proximity-bias story is not supported. Most of the gap comes from eligibility: remote staff are far less likely to have the 18 months in level needed to be nominated (32% of remote staff are eligible versus 74% of office staff). Among eligible employees, remote and office rates are close (20.0% vs 21.1%), and nominees are approved at similar rates (71% vs 74%). A small remaining gap could be chance, since the remote group is only 110 people. Do not announce the three-day office rule. It would penalise remote staff for a cause the data does not show, and it would affect about 180 people who live far away. Next, hold the proposal, and rebuild the reporting to compare eligible remote and office staff. Also look at why remote staff have less time in level, which may reflect recent hiring, and check who gets stretch work, since the current records cannot show it. My confidence in the eligibility finding is moderate-to-good. My confidence about stretch work and attrition is low because we have no data on them.
